description.text: Our mission is to drive Southeast Asia forward by creating economic empowerment for everyone. Our mission is supported by our core principles, which we refer to as the “4Hs,” Heart, Hunger, Honor, and Humility. These principles are set out in The Grab Way, which is a living document that guides our decision making and serves as a reminder of what is important and right as we work to serve Southeast Asia.

about.description_short: Grab is a leading superapp in Southeast Asia, operating across the deliveries, mobility and digital financial services sectors. Serving over 800 cities in eight Southeast Asian countries - Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam - Grab enables millions of people everyday to order food or groceries, send packages, hail a ride or taxi, pay for online purchases or access services such as lending and insurance, all through a single app. We operate supermarkets in Malaysia under Jaya Grocer and Everrise, which enables us to bring the convenience of on-demand grocery delivery to more consumers in the country. As part of our financial services offerings, we also provide digital banking services through GXS Bank in Singapore and GXBank in Malaysia. Grab was founded in 2012 with the mission to drive Southeast Asia forward by creating economic empowerment for everyone.

analysis_md:
# GRAB — Grab Holdings Limited
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-17. In scope (<$40B): market cap (est) $12.366B at $2.94 (nasdaq_quote_api). IFRS filer on Form 20-F (FY2025 filed 2026-03-06).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or segments.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Southeast Asia's leading super-app: Deliveries (FY2025 revenue $1,800M, 53.4% of the $3,370M total), Mobility ($1,219M, 36.2%), Financial Services ($347M, 10.3% — payments, lending, digital banks GXS/GXBank and the Superbank consolidation), Other $4M (segments.json, FY2025 20-F). Listed directly on Nasdaq in Class A ordinary shares via the December 2021 Altimeter SPAC merger. Q2 2026 (6-K earnings release, August 4, 2026): revenue $997M, +22% YoY; on-demand GMV $6.5B, +21%; adjusted EBITDA $168M, +54%; record 54 million monthly transacting users; FY2026 guidance raised to revenue $4.10–4.15B and adjusted EBITDA $720–740M, plus a new $750M buyback authorization.

## Owner's earnings
Conservative OE = OCF − capex − SBC (financials_history.csv):
- FY2023: OCF $86M − capex $71M − SBC $304M = **−$289M (−$0.07/share)**
- FY2024: OCF $852M − capex $77M − SBC $279M = **+$496M (+$0.12/share)** — the only positive year in the last five (OE-positive years 1/5, key_numbers.md)
- FY2025: OCF $79M − capex $97M − SBC $241M = **−$259M (−$0.06/share)**; the maintenance definition (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) is also negative at −$287M, so the verdict does not hinge on the definition.
- **Base used = the normalized base, median of last 3 FY OE/share = −$0.06/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The latest-FY base is the same −$0.06 — median and latest agree that filed OE is negative. No TTM pin: ttm.py reads us-gaap tags only and exits non-zero for this IFRS filer ("no annual (FY) fact" under its candidate tags), so per the worker spec the median base stands. Post-FY press figures were not used as a base: Q2 2026's reported profit of $235M includes a one-off $307M Superbank consolidation gain while operating profit was $19M (Q2 2026 results coverage) — headline TTM profit overstates cash earnings.
- **F sub-type: sbc_exceeds_cash** (key_numbers.md): over the median window OCF − capex is positive, but SBC consumes it. SBC is falling in dollars — $412M (FY2022) → $304M → $279M → $241M (FY2025) — yet FY2025 OCF collapsed to $79M (from $852M), so SBC still swallows the whole cash stream.
- Balance sheet is not the problem: net debt −$1,380M (net cash; cash $3,433M + restricted cash $206M against total borrowings $2,053M, dcf_numbers.json), lease liabilities $234M.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate, real density, unproven cash economics
Justification: Regional density leadership and super-app cross-sell are real but unproven in cash terms: ROIC was negative for FY2021–24 and only barely positive in FY2025, users/drivers/merchants multi-home, and growth is shifting onto a credit balance sheet (lending book, Atome).
- FOR: density leader in Southeast Asia mobility + deliveries (record 54M monthly transacting users in Q2 2026, on-demand GMV +21% YoY); super-app cross-sell on one account/wallet lowers the acquisition cost of each added service; gross margin on the clean post-presentation-change years rose 36.5% (FY2023) → 42.0% (FY2024) → 43.2% (FY2025) per fundamentals.json; net-cash balance sheet (−$1,380M net debt) funds the fintech build-out without forced dilution.
- AGAINST: ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) −29.9% / −17.9% / −9.9% / −3.5% / +0.9% for FY2021–25 — never above the cost of capital in the filed history; multi-homing across GoTo, ShopeeFood/Sea and Foodpanda with near-zero switching costs, and consumer + partner incentives of ~$706M in Q2 2026 alone (Q2 2026 results coverage); growth bought into credit — the scaling lending book and the Atome acquisition ($1.49B initial consideration, September 2026) move risk from take-rate to credit losses, and loan growth absorbs operating cash flow; SBC of $241M against $79M of FY2025 OCF with the share count growing 3.3%/yr; eight-country regulatory patchwork plus ASEAN FX headwinds the company puts at 2–3% inside FY2026 guidance.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth would hold 2 years, then converge linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years — moot this run, since the negative base produces no scenario values.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-17)
Inputs: moat 5, probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — with a negative base the scenario weights cannot change the tier, and no company-specific evidence justifies skewing them), default growth offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp and OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 against the engine's 29.66% blended growth start. Growth sanity check (for the record): the blend's components are rev CAGR 5y 48.36%, rev CAGR 3y 32.97%, latest rev YoY 20.49% (key_numbers.md); current prints are Q2 2026 revenue +22% YoY and FY2026 guidance of $4.10–4.15B against FY2025 revenue of $3,370M — a ~30% base start would sit ABOVE the latest prints, which is one more reason the 5-yr CAGR (an incentive-presentation artifact, see BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT) is not a run-rate. None of it binds: **with base OE/share of −$0.06 the engine produces no scenario IVs or IRRs — tier_by_numbers F, implied_irr_weighted null.**

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | — | 0.75 | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | — | 0.90 | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | — | 1.00 | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | — | 1.10 | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | — | 1.25 | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Final tier: F** (sbc_exceeds_cash). There is no hurdle-clearing price: with negative normalized OE, no purchase price produces a positive owner's-earnings yield on filed numbers — even the one positive year (FY2024, +$0.12/share) is surrounded by negative years and is not a base.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 2025-12-31, 10 months ago): ttm.py cannot compute a TTM base for this IFRS filer (us-gaap tags only; it exited non-zero), so the median base is used per spec. The post-FY evidence is directionally better — Q2 2026 revenue +22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA +54% YoY, FY2026 guidance raised twice — but it is adjusted/press-release evidence, and Q2's reported profit is flattered by the one-off $307M Superbank consolidation gain; it does not convert into a filing-derived OE base. Revisit on the FY2026 20-F.
- **DILUTION** (share count +3.31%/yr, already deducted via the growth adjustment): SBC is falling in dollars ($412M FY2022 → $241M FY2025) but the count still grows on vesting/issuance. The buyback era has only just started ($351M executed by July 2026 under the 2024 authorization, per Q2 2026 coverage; +$750M authorized August 2026) — not yet visible in any filed annual count.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: no divestiture or restatement drives the >60% revenue jumps (FY2021→22 and FY2022→23). They are the incentive-presentation era ending: FY2019 revenue was actually negative (−$845M) because consumer/partner incentives netted against revenue exceeded gross revenue, and revenue "growth" since is largely incentives shrinking as a share of GMV, on top of genuine GMV growth. Consequence: the 48.36% 5-yr revenue CAGR and the early gross margins (−58.5% in FY2021, a nonsensical 95.3% in FY2022 on the tagged COGS) are not comparable to the clean FY2023–25 series (gross margin 36.5% → 43.2%); only the clean years are used for moat evidence. The December 2021 de-SPAC also breaks the share-count basis (see SHARES_FALLBACK).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024): resolved from the FY2025 20-F's audited consolidated statement of cash flows (p. F-10, $ millions) — the gaps are non-cash add-backs plus financial-services balance growth, not a one-off gain. FY2024 (pre-tax loss −$95M → OCF +$852M): deposits from customers in the banking business +$843M was the largest single item, then SBC +$279M, loan receivables −$276M, finance income −$187M, depreciation of PPE +$122M, finance costs +$106M, tax paid −$58M. FY2023 (pre-tax loss −$466M → OCF +$86M): deposits from customers +$364M, SBC +$304M, finance income −$198M, loan receivables −$184M, depreciation +$128M, finance costs +$99M, tax paid −$45M. ## My thoughts / overlay
- This is a "great franchise candidate, no owner's earnings yet" F, not a broken-business F. The operating trajectory is genuinely strong — revenue +20.5% in FY2025, +22% in Q2 2026, adjusted EBITDA margin 16.9% of revenue and compounding for 18 straight quarters, guidance raised twice in 2026 — and the balance sheet carries net cash. What the sweep measures, though, is cash left for owners after SBC and capex, and on filed IFRS numbers that figure has been positive in exactly one of the last five years.
- The swing factor is FY2025's OCF collapse ($852M → $79M) while net income turned positive. If that is mostly loan-book growth (a chosen investment that reverses as the book seasons), forward OE inflects fast; if lending losses and incentive intensity are structural, adjusted EBITDA will keep outrunning cash OE. The Atome deal ($1.49B initial, plus a performance-priced buyout of the remaining 40% ~2 years after close) doubles down on exactly that question, and the market has de-rated the stock ~39% over the three quarters to September 2026 (price $2.94 vs the 52-week high of $6.24) while insider buying (CEO ~$29.9M of Class A shares on 2026-09-21, per insider-trade coverage) goes the other way.
- Method range: every filing-based method lands on F — latest FY −$0.06/share, 3-yr median −$0.06/share, maintenance definition −$287M total. The only route off F is a forward/adjusted construction (guided FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $720–740M minus SBC at the FY2025 level and capex would be solidly positive), which is precisely the construction this method refuses to score. That refusal is the finding: the gap between adjusted EBITDA and owner's earnings IS the investment question on GRAB.
- What would change the tier: an FY2026 20-F (or filing-derived TTM) showing OCF recovering toward the FY2024 level while SBC keeps falling — at FY2024's OE/share (+$0.12) the DCF would still not clear 15% at $2.94, so a re-score needs both cash conversion AND another year of OE growth, not just one good print.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F, no override; F sub-type sbc_exceeds_cash)
- Confidence: **Low** (high on the filed OE arithmetic — both definitions negative, median and latest bases agree; low on how fast the lending-book cash absorption reverses, which decides the next score)
- One-liner: Southeast Asia's leading super-app, moat 5/10 — Tier F on numbers: normalized owner's earnings are negative (-$0.06/share) because SBC ($241M in FY2025) exceeds what thin operating cash flow leaves after capex, so it clears no hurdle at $2.94 on filed OE; the bull case rests on adjusted-EBITDA growth (Q2 2026 +54% YoY, FY2026 guidance raised) converting into cash owner's earnings, which the filings have not yet shown.
